title: Communication Skills (1B checklist)
sourceNote: Sections follow the 1B communication checklist (V2); every label is paraphrased in our own words. The pass threshold is a placeholder pending faculty confirmation.

items.label: Greets the patient by name
items.guidance: Student greets the patient and uses the patient’s name (any form, e.g. Mr./Ms. + surname or first name if invited).

patterns: \b(?:hi|hello|hey|good (?:morning|afternoon|evening)|nice to meet you|pleased to meet you|welcome)\b.*\b(?:mr|mrs|ms|miss|mx)\b
exemplars: Hello Mr. Bennett, nice to meet you.
Good morning, Mrs. Garcia.
Hi, are you Mr. Bennett?
Hello Harold, is it okay if I call you Harold?
Good afternoon Ms. Okafor, thanks for waiting.
Hi there, Mr. Lee, how are you doing today?
Mr. Bennett? Hello, it's nice to meet you.
Hello, you must be Mr. Bennett.
counterExemplars: Hello, how are you today?
Hi, my name is Alex and I'm a first-year medical student.
Good morning!
Can you tell me your full name and date of birth?

items.label: Says they are a first-year medical student
items.guidance: Credit if the student tells the patient they are a first-year (or first year) medical student. Half credit for "medical student" without the year.

exemplars: I'm a first-year medical student.
I'm a first year med student working with the team today.
My name is Sam and I'm a first-year student at the medical school.
I'm in my first year of medical school.
I'm one of the first-year medical students here.
I'm a first-year student doctor, and I'll be talking with you before the doctor comes in.
I'm a 1st year medical student.
counterExemplars: I'm a medical student.
I'm a third-year medical student.
I'm a student doctor working with the team.
Is this your first time in the emergency department?

items.label: Removes barriers to communication (sits down at eye level)
Checks comfort, readiness and privacy; puts patient at ease
items.guidance: Student asks whether the patient is comfortable / ready, or addresses privacy, or makes a remark that puts the patient at ease.

patterns: \b(?:are you|you are|you|is that|is everything) (?:sitting |feeling |still )?(?:comfortable|comfy)\b(?!.*\b(?:at night|when you (?:sleep|lie)|sleeping|in bed|lying flat|lie flat|overnight)\b)
exemplars: Are you comfortable sitting like that?
Is now a good time for us to talk?
Would you like me to close the curtain for some privacy?
Before we start, can I get you anything to make you more comfortable?
Is it alright if I ask you some questions about what's been going on?
Are you ready to get started, or do you need a moment?
Take your time, there's no rush at all.
Are you warm enough? I can grab you a blanket.
Let me pull the curtain so we have a bit more privacy.
counterExemplars: How are you today?
Are you comfortable lying flat at night?
Does anything make your breathing more comfortable?
Have you been sleeping comfortably?

items.label: Elicits chief concern with an open-ended question
items.guidance: An open question to elicit the main concern (e.g. What brings you in today?). Closed questions do not count.
mockKeywords: what can i do for you

keywords: what can i do for you
what can we do for you
what seems to be the problem
what seems to be the trouble
patterns: \bwhat (?:is|has been) (?:going on|bothering you|troubling you|the problem|the matter)\b
\bwhat would you like to (?:talk about|discuss) today\b
exemplars: What brings you in today?
What brought you to the emergency department?
How can I help you today?
So, tell me what's been going on.
What's been bothering you?
Can you tell me what brought you in today?
What made you decide to come to the hospital today?
What would you like to talk about today?
What can we do for you this morning?
counterExemplars: Are you here because of your breathing?
So you're here for shortness of breath, is that right?
Is it your chest that's bothering you?
What do you think is causing this?

items.label: Elicits additional concerns with an open-ended question
items.guidance: Asks whether there is anything else the patient wants to address today, before diving into the HPI.

keywords: anything else you would like to talk about
anything else you would like to discuss
anything else you wanted to talk about
anything else you wanted to discuss
anything else you would like to cover
something else you would like to discuss
something else you wanted to discuss
patterns: \b(?:anything|something) else (?:that )?(?:you would like|you wanted|you want|you were hoping|we should|i should know about today|on your mind|bothering you|you are (?:worried|concerned) about|to (?:talk about|discuss|cover|add|bring up|address))\b
\bwhat else (?:would you like|did you want|do you want|were you hoping|is (?:on your mind|bothering you)|are you (?:worried|concerned) about|brings you)\b
\b(?:apart from|besides|other than|in addition to|aside from)\b.*\b(?:anything|something|what) else\b
^(?:(?:and|so|ok|okay|alright|right|now|before we start) )*(?:is there |was there )?(?:anything|something) else(?: today)?$
exemplars: Before we get into that, is there anything else you'd like to talk about today?
Is there something else you were hoping to discuss while you're here?
What else would you like to cover today?
Are there any other concerns you'd like to bring up?
Besides your breathing, is there anything else on your mind?
Apart from that, what else did you want to talk about?
Anything else bothering you that we should address today?
Is there anything else?
counterExemplars: Any other symptoms?
Does anything else make it worse?
Do you have any other questions for me before I go?
Do you have any other medical conditions?

items.label: Notes additional issues to discuss today
items.guidance: Acknowledges/lists the additional issues raised so they are not lost (e.g. We will also talk about X).

patterns: \b(?:we|i) (?:will|can|should|are going to|shall) (?:also |definitely |make sure to |make sure we )?(?:talk about|discuss|come back to|get to|cover|address|go over) (?:that|those|both|it|this|them|the|your)\b

\b(?:i will|let me|i am going to|i have|i just want to|i will just) (?:make a note of (?:that|this|it|your|the|those)|make a note so|note (?:that|this|it|your|the|those) (?:down|too|as well)|noted (?:that|this|it|your|the|those)|jot (?:that|this|it) down|write (?:that|this|it|those) down)\b
exemplars: Okay, so we'll talk about your breathing and we'll also get to the ankle swelling.
I'll make a note of that so we can come back to it.
Let me write that down so we don't forget to discuss it.
So we have your breathing and your cough, and we'll cover both today.
Got it, we'll make sure to talk about your sleep as well.
I've noted the leg swelling too; we'll come back to that in a bit.
So the main things today are your breathing and the swelling in your legs.
counterExemplars: I'm going to jot down a few notes while we talk, if that's alright.
Okay.
Let's go back to when the breathing started.

items.label: Prioritises concerns if necessary
items.guidance: If more than one concern exists, negotiates which to focus on first. If the patient raised only one concern, score 1 only if the student explicitly confirmed there was nothing else to prioritise; otherwise 0.

keywords: nothing else you wanted to discuss
nothing else you would like to discuss
patterns: \b(?:would you like|do you want|should we|shall we|can we|let us|could we|is it ok(?:ay)? if we|i would like to|i suggest we|we will|we can|we could) (?:to )?(?:start|begin|focus|concentrate) (?:with|on)\b
\b(?:so )?(?:it is|is it|is that) (?:just|only) (?:the|your)\b.*\b(?:today|you want|you would like|you wanted)\b
exemplars: Which of those would you like to start with?
Since your breathing seems to bother you most, shall we focus on that first?
Would it be okay if we start with the breathing and then talk about the cough?
What's most important for you to sort out today?
So it's just the breathing you want to focus on today, nothing else?
Just to confirm, there's nothing else you'd like to discuss besides your breathing?
Let's start with your breathing since that sounds most pressing, and then we'll get to the swelling.
Of the things you mentioned, which one worries you the most?
counterExemplars: Did it start with a cough?
When did it start?
Is there anything that makes it better?

items.label: Invites the patient’s story with an open-ended prompt
items.guidance: Invites the patient’s narrative with an open prompt (e.g. Tell me about…).

keywords: tell me what has been happening
tell me what has been going on
patterns: \b(?:could|can|would) you (?:please )?(?:describe|tell me about|walk me through|talk me through) (?:what|how|it|this|that|everything|your|the)\b
exemplars: Tell me more about your breathing.
Can you walk me through what's been happening over the last couple of weeks?
Start from the beginning and tell me what's been going on.
Could you describe what the breathlessness has been like for you?
Tell me all about it.
In your own words, what has this been like?
Take me back to when this all started and tell me how it's gone since.
I'd like to hear the whole story, starting from when you first noticed it.
counterExemplars: Is it worse when you walk?
When did it start?
Can you tell me your full name?
Do you get short of breath at night?

items.label: Uses paraverbal encouragement and silence
items.notAssessableReason: Needs voice timing and body language; not measured yet (silence could later come from voice timing).

items.label: Uses a second or third open question / echoing to get more story
items.guidance: After the first answer, uses another open prompt or echoes the patient’s words to invite more.

patterns: ^(?:(?:ok|okay|mm|hmm|mhm|right|i see) )*(?:go on|please go on|keep going|carry on|please continue)$
exemplars: Tell me more about that.
Go on.
What else have you noticed?
And then what happened?
Okay, and how has it been since then?
You said you can't catch your breath; can you tell me more about that?
What happened after that?
Can you say a bit more about what happens at night?
Can't lie flat?
counterExemplars: Does anything else make it worse?
Is it worse at night?
Do you have any allergies?

items.label: Clarifies by summarising
items.guidance: Summarises or checks understanding (e.g. Let me make sure I have this right…).

keywords: let me see if i have
correct me if i am wrong
just to make sure i understand
let me see if i understand
patterns: \b(?:let me|i want to|i would like to|just want to|just to) (?:make sure|check|confirm|clarify|see if) (?:i|that i)? ?(?:have|got|understand|understood|heard|have got|am understanding)\b
\bso (?:you are saying|what you are saying is|you said|if i (?:understand|heard))\b
exemplars: Let me make sure I have this right: you've been more short of breath for about two weeks?
So what I'm hearing is that it's been getting worse, especially at night.
Just to recap, you ran out of your water pill about ten days ago.
If I understand correctly, you need three pillows to sleep now.
So you're saying the swelling started about a week ago, is that right?
Correct me if I'm wrong, but it sounds like the breathing is worse when you lie down.
Just to clarify, did you say the cough is dry?
Okay, so far I've got breathlessness, swollen ankles and a dry cough.
counterExemplars: Can you tell me more about the cough?
What do you think is going on?
Sorry, could you repeat that? I didn't catch it.

items.label: Elicits emotional context
items.guidance: Asks how the problem is affecting the patient emotionally / how they are coping.

keywords: how has this made you feel
how does that make you feel
how does this make you feel
what is this like for you
what has this been like for you
patterns: \b(?:are you|is anything|is something|what is|what are you|is there anything you are|have you been) (?:most |been )?(?:worried|worrying|anxious|scared|concerned|frightened|stressed|upset|nervous)\b
exemplars: How are you feeling about all of this?
How have you been coping with the breathlessness?
Is anything about this worrying you?
What's been the hardest part of this for you?
How has this made you feel?
That sounds scary. How are you holding up?
What worries you most about what's been happening?
Has all this been stressful for you?
counterExemplars: How are you feeling today?
Do you feel short of breath right now?
Have you been feeling low or depressed lately?
Have you had any chest pain?

items.label: Elicits personal context
items.guidance: Asks what the problem means for the patient’s life (work, family, activities, roles).

keywords: what does this mean for you
patterns: \bwhat (?:can you not|are you not able to|can you no longer|could you do before|have you had to (?:stop|give up))\b
exemplars: How has this been affecting your day-to-day life?
Has the breathlessness stopped you from doing the things you enjoy?
How is this impacting things at home with your family?
What can't you do now that you could do a month ago?
Has this affected your ability to get around or look after yourself?
What does all this mean for you and your plans this week?
How has this changed your routine?
Is it getting in the way of spending time with your grandchildren?
counterExemplars: Does anyone in your family have heart problems?
Who do you live with at home?
What do you do for work?
Has it been getting worse over time?

items.label: Responds to emotional or personal context (empathy)
items.guidance: Explicitly acknowledges or validates the patient’s feelings or situation.

keywords: that is a lot to deal with
patterns: \b(?:that|it|this|all this|all of that) (?:sounds|must be|must have been|seems|has been) (?:really |very |so |quite |pretty |incredibly )?(?:hard|difficult|tough|scary|frightening|frustrating|worrying|stressful|exhausting|upsetting|awful|overwhelming|challenging|a lot|distressing|uncomfortable)\b
\b(?:it is|that is|it is completely|that is completely|it is totally|that is totally|it is very|that is very|it is really|that is really|very) understandable\b
\b(?:i am|i am really|i am so|i am very) sorry (?:to hear|that you|you are|you have|about (?:that|this|all))\b
exemplars: That sounds really frightening.
I can imagine how exhausting that must be.
I'm sorry you've been going through this.
It's completely understandable that you're worried about missing the birthday.
That must be really hard, not being able to sleep lying down.
No wonder you're feeling worn out.
It makes sense that you'd be scared it's your heart again.
Thank you for telling me that; I know it isn't easy to talk about.
counterExemplars: That sounds like it could be fluid on your lungs.
I'm sorry, could you repeat that?
Okay, got it. And when did the swelling start?

items.label: Clarifies the timeline
items.guidance: Establishes when it started and how it evolved over time.

keywords: how long has this been going on
how long has it been going on
exemplars: When did this all start?
How long has this been going on?
Has it been getting worse, better, or staying the same?
How has it changed over the past two weeks?
Walk me through how it's progressed since it started.
Was it sudden, or did it build up gradually?
When did you first notice the swelling, and has it changed since?
What was it like at the beginning compared with now?
counterExemplars: When did you have your heart attack?
How long have you been taking carvedilol?
When did you last take your water pill?

items.label: Onset
items.guidance: Asks how the symptom began (sudden vs gradual, what they were doing).

patterns: \b(?:sudden|suddenly|gradual|gradually|all at once|out of the blue|overnight|creep up|crept up)\b
exemplars: Did it come on suddenly or gradually?
How did it first start?
What were you doing when you first noticed it?
Was it all at once, or did it creep up on you?
When did the breathlessness begin?
Can you remember when you first noticed it?
Did it start out of the blue?
When did you first start feeling short of breath?
counterExemplars: When did you start taking furosemide?
When did you stop taking your water pill?
When did your heart attack happen?

items.label: Duration
items.guidance: Asks how long the symptom has been present / how long episodes last.

keywords: how long has this been going on
how long has it been going on
how long have you been short of breath
how long does each episode last
exemplars: How long has this been going on?
How long have you been short of breath?
How many days has your breathing been like this?
How long do the episodes at night last?
When you wake up gasping, how long does it take to settle?
So it's been going on for about two weeks?
How long have your ankles been swollen?
For how long have you had the cough?
counterExemplars: How long did you smoke for?
How long have you been taking carvedilol?
How long can you walk before you need to stop?

items.label: Quality
items.guidance: Asks what the symptom feels like.

keywords: what does the breathlessness feel like
patterns: \bdescribe (?:the|what the|how the|what it|how it|what that|how that) (?:\w+ )?(?:feels?|feeling|sensation|like|is like)\b
\b(?:cannot|not able to|unable to) (?:get enough air|catch your breath|get a full breath|take a deep breath)\b.*\bor\b
exemplars: What does the breathlessness feel like?
How would you describe the feeling?
Is it more like you can't get enough air, or a tightness in your chest?
Can you describe what the cough is like?
What kind of feeling is it: tight, heavy, or something else?
Is the cough dry, or are you bringing anything up?
When you say you're winded, what does that feel like for you?
What does it feel like when you wake up at night?
counterExemplars: How do you feel today?
How are you feeling about all this?
Do you feel short of breath right now?

items.label: Quantification / severity
items.guidance: Quantifies severity or functional impact (scale, distance walked, number of pillows, etc.).

keywords: how far are you able to walk
patterns: \bhow (?:far|many blocks|many steps|many flights|long|much) (?:can|could|are|were|do|did) you (?:walk|go|climb|manage|able to walk|able to go|get)\b
\b(?:can|are you able to|could|do you manage to) (?:you )?(?:climb|walk up|manage|get up) (?:a |one |the )?(?:flight of |few )?(?:stairs|steps)\b
exemplars: How far can you walk before you have to stop?
On a scale of one to ten, how bad is your breathing?
How many pillows do you sleep on?
Can you manage a flight of stairs?
How many blocks could you walk two weeks ago compared with now?
How much has it limited what you can do?
Are you able to get dressed without getting winded?
How severe would you say it is right now?
counterExemplars: How many children do you have?
How many cigarettes a day did you smoke?
How much do you drink in a week?

items.label: Related symptoms
items.guidance: Asks about associated symptoms.

patterns: \b(?:along with|alongside|together with|at the same time as|accompanied by|apart from|besides|as well as) (?:the |your |that |this )?(?:breath\w*|shortness|cough\w*|pain|symptoms?|swelling|it|this|that)\b.*\b(?:noticed|notice|symptoms?|feel|felt|experienc\w*|happen\w*|had|having|get|getting)\b

\b(?:noticed|symptoms?|feel|felt|experienc\w*|had|having)\b.*\b(?:along with|alongside|together with|at the same time as|accompanied by|apart from|besides|as well as) (?:the |your |that |this )?(?:breath\w*|shortness|cough\w*|pain|swelling|it|this|that)\b
exemplars: Have you noticed any other symptoms along with the breathlessness?
Any swelling in your legs or ankles?
Have you had a cough?
Does anything else happen when you get short of breath, like chest pain or dizziness?
Have you noticed any weight gain?
Any fevers or chills?
Have you been waking up at night short of breath?
Is there anything else you've noticed that seems related?
counterExemplars: Do you have any other medical conditions?
Any other concerns you want to discuss today?
Do you have any other questions for me?

items.label: Setting
items.guidance: Asks the setting in which it occurs (exertion, lying flat, time of day, at night).

keywords: when do you notice it most
patterns: \b(?:worse|better|happen|happens|come on|comes on|notice it|get it|get them|bother you|bothers you|breathless|short of breath|winded)\b.*\b(?:at night|in the morning|in the evening|during the day|at rest|when you (?:lie|walk|exert|exercise|climb|sleep|rest|bend|are (?:walking|resting|lying|climbing)))\b
exemplars: Is it worse when you lie flat?
Do you get short of breath at night?
Does it happen when you're walking, or also at rest?
Is there a particular time of day when it's worse?
Do you notice it more when you're climbing stairs?
Have you ever woken up at night struggling to breathe?
When do you notice it most?
What are you usually doing when you get breathless?
counterExemplars: Do you get up at night to pass urine?
Do you walk for exercise?
Where do you live?

items.label: Transforming factors
items.guidance: Asks what makes it better or worse.

exemplars: Does anything make it better?
What makes it worse?
Is there anything that helps you breathe easier?
Does sitting up help?
Have you tried anything to relieve it?
Does resting make it go away?
What brings it on?
Is it better or worse when you lie down?
counterExemplars: Has it been getting better or worse over time?
Are you feeling any better today?
Do you feel better than you did yesterday?

items.label: Uses closed questions to narrow the differential
items.guidance: Asks specific yes/no questions aimed at raising or lowering particular diagnoses (e.g. chest pain, fever, leg pain, medication adherence).

patterns: \b(?:any|have you had|have you noticed|do you have|did you have|have you been having)\b.*\b(?:chest (?:pain|tightness|pressure)|fevers?|chills|calf|calves|leg pain|blood|palpitations|racing|skipping|faint|fainted|passed out|dizzy|wheez\w*|sputum|phlegm)\b
exemplars: Have you had any chest pain?
Any fevers or chills?
Have you noticed any pain or swelling in your calves?
Have you been taking all your medications as prescribed?
Have you missed any doses of your water pill?
Have you coughed up any blood?
Have you eaten a lot of salty food recently?
Any recent long flights or car trips?
Have you felt your heart racing or skipping beats?
Did you have a cold or chest infection before this started?
counterExemplars: Tell me about your medications.
What makes it worse?
What other symptoms have you noticed?

items.label: Summarises the HPI and checks accuracy
items.guidance: Gives a summary of the HPI back to the patient and asks if it is accurate.

keywords: let me go over what you have told me
patterns: \b(?:let me|i would like to|i want to|so just to|just to|so to|to|let us|i will|i am going to) (?:quickly )?(?:summarize|summarise|recap|sum up|go over what|run through what|review what)\b
\bis (?:that|this|all that|all of that|everything) (?:an )?(?:accurate|a fair|a good|a correct)(?: summary| picture)?\b
\b(?:is there )?anything (?:i (?:missed|left out|got wrong|have missed|have left out|have got wrong))\b
exemplars: So, to summarize: for the past two weeks you've been getting more short of breath, you need three pillows to sleep, and your ankles have been swelling. Did I get that right?
Let me recap what you've told me so far, and you tell me if I've missed anything.
Just to make sure I have the whole picture: the breathing started two weeks ago and has got worse, especially at night. Is that accurate?
Before we move on, let me go over what you've told me.
Okay, so it's breathlessness getting worse over two weeks, worse lying flat, with swollen ankles and a dry cough. Have I got that right?
Did I miss anything important?
Is there anything I left out or got wrong?
counterExemplars: Is that right, you have a dry cough?
Did you say three pillows?
Can you tell me more about that?

items.label: Signposts the move to more directed questions
items.guidance: Tells the patient they will now ask about past history / other questions.

keywords: now i would like to ask
i would like to move on to
next i would like to ask
patterns: \b(?:now|next|at this point|moving on)\b.*\b(?:i would like to|i want to|i am going to|i will|let me|let us|we will|i need to)\b.*\b(?:ask|talk about|go over|move on|switch|learn)\b
exemplars: Now I'd like to ask you some questions about your past health.
Thank you, that's really helpful. Next I'm going to ask about your medications and your family.
I'm going to switch gears a bit and ask some more general questions.
Let's move on to your medical history.
I'm going to ask a series of quick yes-or-no questions about other parts of your body.
Now I want to learn a bit more about your background, if that's okay.
Next, I'd like to ask about your lifestyle and home life.
I have a few more questions about your general health.
counterExemplars: Now I'd like to examine you, if that's okay.
Do you have any questions for me?
Can I ask what brings you in today?

items.label: Transitions to the physical exam
items.guidance: Tells the patient they will now examine them and asks permission.

patterns: \b(?:i would like to|i am going to|i will|i want to|i need to|let me|may i|can i|could i|is it ok(?:ay)? if i|would it be ok(?:ay)? if i|is it alright if i|do you mind if i|would you mind if i|we will|we are going to)\b.*\b(?:examine|examination|exam|listen to your (?:heart|chest|lungs|breathing)|take a look at your|check your (?:heart|chest|lungs|legs|ankles|belly))\b
\b(?:would you mind if i|do you mind if i|may i|can i|is it ok(?:ay)? if i) (?:listened|listen|looked|look|felt|feel|pressed|press|checked|check)\b
exemplars: Now I'd like to do a physical exam, is that okay with you?
If it's alright, I'm going to examine you now.
Would you mind if I listened to your heart and lungs?
Next I'll do a quick examination; let me know if anything is uncomfortable.
Is it okay if we move on to the physical exam?
I'd like to take a look at your legs and listen to your chest, if that's all right.
May I examine you now?
We're going to move on to the exam part now. Are you okay with that?
counterExemplars: Has a doctor examined you recently?
Now I'd like to ask some questions about your past medical history.
Did they do an exam when you came in?

items.label: Shares impressions in plain language, without deferring
items.guidance: Near the end, the student shares their impression of what may be going on, in plain language the patient can follow. Half credit if they use unexplained medical jargon (e.g. "decompensated", "HFrEF", "edema" without explanation). Zero if they only defer ("my attending will decide", "the doctor will tell you") without sharing any impression.
mockKeywords: what i think is going on

keywords: what i think is going on
from what you have told me

items.label: Explains next steps in plain language
items.guidance: The student tells the patient what happens next (further tests, who they will see) in plain language. 1B has no management plan: credit next steps, not treatment decisions. Zero if they defer every question.

keywords: will come in to see you
will come in and see you
